thread.title: Stocks Rally On China Trade War Talks; Apple iPhones Unveiled; Tilray, Nio IPOs Soar: Weekly Review | Investor's Business Daily

author: IBD STAFF
title: Stocks Rally On China Trade War Talks; Apple iPhones Unveiled; Tilray, Nio IPOs Soar: Weekly Review | Investor's Business Daily

organizations.name: stocks rally on china trade war talks

text:
The Dow Jones and other major averages rallied during the week, as U.S.-China trade tensions eased. Apple ( AAPL ) unveiled expensive new iPhones as well as an enhanced, larger Apple Watch. Chip stocks broke support, but rebounded for modest gains. China stocks rebounded, with would-be Tesla ( TSLA ) rival Nio ( NIO ) soaring in its IPO. Tilray ( TLRY ), the first true U.S.-listed marijuana stock IPO, vaulted higher.
Stocks Rally On China Trade Talks X
The major averages rallied on a Tuesday report that the U.S. had called for new trade talks with China, though President Donald Trump reportedly wants to go ahead with tariffs on a further $200 billion in Chinese goods. That buoyed U.S.-listed China stocks and helped spur a rebound in chip stocks. Apple ( AAPL ) stock rallied for the week after it unveiled new iPhones and other products. China luxury electric vehicle maker Nio ( NIO ) priced its IPO low, but shares soared for the week. Recent marijuana IPO Tilray ( TLRY ) broke on through to the other side of 100 despite claims that it couldn't get much higher.
Apple Unleashes iPhone XS Consumer electronics giant Apple ( AAPL ) introduced three 12th-generation iPhones and a fourth-generation Apple Watch at its fall product launch event on Wednesday. The new handsets include the 5.8-inch OLED-screen iPhone XS, 6.5-inch OLED-screen iPhone XS Max and 6.1-inch LCD-screen iPhone XR. Wall Street was surprised by higher-than-expected prices for the new handsets. The Apple Watch Series 4 stole the show in the eyes of many analysts. The new smartwatch includes enhanced health and fitness features, such as both optical and electrical heart-rate sensors. Also, the watch display is over 30% bigger than its predecessor. Apple shares rose 1.15% for the week, near record highs.
Chip Stocks Volatile Semiconductor stocks overall have been poor performers lately on concerns ranging from slowing smartphone sales to weakening memory-chip markets. Micron Technology ( MU ) fell hard Wednesday on worries about declining DRAM memory chip prices and it pulled down semiconductor equipment stocks. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index undercut its 200-day moving average intraday Wednesday, but rebounded to close higher, above its 50-day line. AMD ( AMD ) and Nvidia ( NVDA ) have outperformed their peers because they play into the hot data center and graphics chip markets. Japanese chipmaker Renesas agreed to buy Integrated Device Technology ( IDTI ) for $6.7 billion, raising the prospect of more chip M&A activity.
Tilray IPO Smokes Tilray ( TLRY ), a pot producer in Canada that went public on the Nasdaq this summer, spiked 40% for the week, even as short-seller Citron Research raised concerns about lofty valuations. Shares of Tilray retreated Friday after a U.S. Customs official said Canadian marijuana industry workers and investors could face a lifetime travel ban to the U.S., a reminder that cannabis products are still illegal under federal law. Tilray also said it acquired the permits to export dry medical marijuana to Germany, and that a nonpsychoactive product "was successfully imported" into the U.K. for a patient with epilepsy. Meanwhile, a SunTrust analyst saw "little certainty" in Corona parent Constellation Brands ' ( STZ ) $4 billion investment in Canadian marijuana producer Canopy Growth ( CGC ), and said it would "keep a cloud over the stock (pun intended) for at least the next few quarters."
Moonves Resigns Amid Mounting Accusations CBS ( CBS ) CEO and Chairman Les Moonves resigned Sunday, Sept. 9, after six more women accused him of sexual harassment or assault. Moonves has a $120 million severance coming, but only if a CBS probe clears him of wrongdoing. Moonves' exit is part of a broader deal with National Amusements, which is the controlling shareholder of CBS, and Viacom ( VIAB ). CBS will shake up its board while National Amusements agreed not to pursue a CBS-Viacom merger for 18 months. Also, a top CBS "60 Minutes" producer was fired over his handling of sexual harassment claims. CBS stock edged lower after soaring in the prior week on reports of the broader deal. Viacom rose 3%.
Hurricane Stocks Home Depot ( HD ) stock held in a buy zone while Lowe's ( LOW ) hit a record high. Generator maker Generac ( GNRC ) broke out ahead of Hurricane Florence slamming into the Carolinas, but then pulled back to end the week slightly above the entry point. Investors were betting on pre- and post-storm sales. Insurers are expected to suffer losses due to storm damage. But Allstate ( ALL ) and other property and casualty insurer stocks didn't move much.
Adobe Earnings Beat Q3 Views Digital media and marketing software firm Adobe Systems ( ADBE ) late Thursday earned an adjusted $1.73 a share, up 57%, on sales of $2.29 billion, up 24%, in the third quarter ended Aug. 31. Analysts expected EPS of $1.69 on sales of $2.25 billion. For the current Q4, Adobe guided just above views. Adobe expects to earn an adjusted $1.87 a share on sales of $2.42 billion. Wall Street was modeling Adobe to earn $1.86 a share on sales of $2.41 billion. Reuters reported that Adobe is in talks to buy cloud marketing software company Marketo. Adobe stock rose Friday, staying in buy range.
Crude Prices Rise Amid Falling Inventories, Output Brent crude futures briefly topped $80 a barrel. U.S. crude futures moved above $70 but then settled back to close with a 1.8% gain at $68.99. The Energy Information Administration reported a 5.3 million barrel drop in U.S. crude stockpiles Wednesday, twice as much as expected. OPEC cut its 2019 demand growth outlook on economic uncertainty in Latin America and the Middle East, in its monthly oil market report also out Wednesday. But Brent oil prices could top $80 per barrel if Venezuelan and Iranian exports continue to fall and production elsewhere doesn't step up, the International Energy Agency reported in its oil market report Thursday.
Boeing Bullish On 737 Deliveries Boeing ( BA ) delivered 48 737s in August, up from 29 in the prior month, and CEO Dennis Muilenburg said September deliveries will be flat to slightly up. The Dow Jones giant is on track to deliver more planes in Q4. Muilenburg said that the aerospace giant hasn't seen a material impact from the trade war with China. Over the next 20 years, Boeing expects China to need 7,690 new airplanes valued at $1.2 trillion. That's up 6% from the number of jets Boeing estimated in a prior forecast. The Air Force awarded the aircraft maker a $2.9 billion KC-46 tanker contract, offering a vote of confidence in the program ahead of an initial delivery pushed back by repeated delays. Boeing stock rose, helped by easing China trade tensions.
Kroger Dives On Weak Sales Kroger ( KR ) earnings topped second-quarter views, but revenue missed some estimates and same-store sales came in light. Digital sales jumped 50%. Kroger reiterated EPS guidance, which was just OK. The grocery-store operator said it was "aggressively investing" in digital shopping services — an effort to compete with the likes of Amazon ( AMZN ) and Walmart ( WMT ). Kroger stock, which had been slightly extended from a buy point, plunged 9.9% Thursday.
Tesla Stock Tesla ( TSLA ) was slammed by one of its biggest bulls, who slashed his price target and bemoaned the erratic behavior of Chief Executive Elon Musk. Longtime Tesla bull Romit Shah at Nomura cut his price target on Tesla by 25%, to 300 from 400. He also moved his rating to neutral, from buy. Meanwhile, Loup Ventures analyst Gene Munster said Tesla may not survive without big changes, starting with overhauling the board of directors. Musk said customer deliveries could be delayed due to increased production volumes. Tesla stock jumped 12% after crashing in recent weeks.
Economic Data Just Right U.S. economic data remained just about perfect. Retail sales were stronger than they appeared while inflation was softer than expected. Core consumer price inflation rose a tame 0.1% in August, leaving the core CPI up 2.2% from a year ago. That trailed views for 2.3% inflation and July's 2.4% annual rate. The overall CPI, including food and energy prices, rose 0.2% on the month and 2.7% from a year ago. Headline retail sales gains of 0.1% overall and 0.3% excluding autos missed views. But July data were revised up. Compared to a year ago, retail sales rose 6.6% overall and 7.3% excluding autos.
News In Brief Pivotal Software ( PVTL ) reported a narrower-than-expected loss as revenue rose 30% to $164 million, also topping views. But calculated billings of $133 million missed estimates by $25 million, sending shares in the enterprise software maker plummeting.
Tesla ( TSLA ) China rival Nio 's ( NIO ) stock exploded after a challenging IPO trading debut that saw it fall as low as 5.35, far below its 6.26 initial price. It recovered to close up, and gained 58% in its first week.
Stryker ( SYK ) agreed to buy Invuity for $190 million. Invuity makes lighted instruments for surgeries. The deal is expected to close in the fourth quarter.
Gilead Sciences ( GILD ) and Galapagos ( GLPG ) announced their rheumatoid arthritis drug, filgotinib, met their key goals in a study of patients who previously had inadequate responses to other biologic drugs. Gilead stock rose 2.4% Wednesday, and Galapagos leapt 16.5%, hitting a record high.
Google ( GOOGL ), Facebook ( FB ) and Twitter ( TWTR ) must remove extremist content within an hour or face hefty fines, the European Commission's president said in his annual state of the union address to the European Parliament. All three stocks are struggling to keep up with the general market. Snapchat parent Snap ( SNAP ) fell to a record low as an analyst slashed its price target to 5.
Sonos ( SONO ) saw shares plummet 22% Tuesday after the wireless speaker maker reported disappointing results for its first quarter as a publicly traded company.
